messages.text: Sabalenka beats Rakhimova to reach fourth round of US Open

metadata.summary: Aryna Sabalenka came through a tough test against Kamilla Rakhimova - particularly in the second set - to reach the fourth round of the US Open.
metadata.content: US Open: Aryna Sabalenka beats Kamilla Rakhimova in straight sets to reach fourth round in Flushing Meadows | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open: Aryna Sabalenka beats Kamilla Rakhimova in straight sets to reach fourth round in Flushing Meadows Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka comes through in straight sets against Kamilla Rakhimova, the world No 1 winning 6-3 6-4; watch US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, on NOW and the Sky Sports app Friday 4 September 2026 17:59, UK Image: Aryna Sabalenka is through to the last 16 of the US Open after a straight-sets win over Kamilla Rakhimova Aryna Sabalenka came through a tough test against Kamilla Rakhimova - particularly in the second set - to reach the fourth round of the US Open. The two-time defending champion in New York started superbly, storming into a 3-0 lead in the opening set as she didn't miss a single first serve until the seventh game of the match, in which Rakhimova would three times take her to deuce. That would prove to be Rakhimova's only real opening in the first set, Sabalenka taking it 6-3, but she'd prove much more competitive in the second. messages.text: Russell tops second practice as Mercedes respond to Ferrari at Monza

metadata.summary: George Russell beat Charles Leclerc to the fastest time of second practice at the Italian Grand Prix as Mercedes responded to Ferrari's early pace at Monza.
metadata.content: Italian GP: George Russell fastest in Practice Two as Mercedes edge ahead of fast-starting Ferrari at Monza | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Italian GP: George Russell fastest in Practice Two as Mercedes edge ahead of fast-starting Ferrari at Monza George Russell starts a big weekend in which Kimi Antonelli takes a grid penalty by setting Friday's fastest time at The Temple of Speed; Charles Leclerc leads Ferrari in second; watch final practice at 11.30am on Saturday ahead of Qualifying at 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Friday 4 September 2026 17:20, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Italian Grand Prix. George Russell beat Charles Leclerc to the fastest time of second practice at the Italian Grand Prix as Mercedes responded to Ferrari's early pace at Monza. At an event in which championship-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli will start at the back of Sunday's grid owing to engine-change penalties, Russell has a big chance to eat into the Italian's 59-point advantage if he can deliver a strong race weekend. Ferrari had finished first and second quickest in opening practice as they debuted an upgraded engine but Russell was the driver to beat in the second session amid continued sweltering temperatures in northern Italy. messages.text: Hearn: Talks 'reopened' for Fury vs AJ at Wembley

metadata.summary: Promoter Eddie Hearn has announced that talks have "reopened" to stage the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium.
metadata.content: Fury vs Joshua: Eddie Hearn says talks have 'reopened' to stage British heavyweight blockbuster at Wembley Stadium | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Fury vs Joshua: Eddie Hearn says talks have 'reopened' to stage British heavyweight blockbuster at Wembley Stadium A long-awaited blockbuster fight between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury has been stuck in negotiations in recent months amid an apparent disagreement over the location for the event, Joshua's team having remained insistent it must take place in the United Kingdom Friday 4 September 2026 17:16, UK Image: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury could finally settle their rivalry at Wembley Stadium Promoter Eddie Hearn has announced that talks have "reopened" to stage the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium. Negotiations for the Fury vs Joshua fight had hit a major stumbling block after Madison Square Garden in New York emerged as the preferred venue to stage the blockbuster bout. But Hearn has released a statement on social media, revealing that Wembley is again being considered as the venue for the fight. He wrote: "I want to thank everyone for the unbelievable support!" "You have been heard and talks have now re-opened for Wembley. "Let's make history with one of the biggest sporting moments [British flag] has ever seen." messages.text: Arrow gets emotional farewell on 100th Rabbitohs appearance after MND diagnosis

metadata.summary: Jai Arrow made an emotional 100th NRL appearance for the South Sydney Rabbitohs to mark his farewell from the sport, following his Motor Neurone Disease diagnosis.
metadata.content: Jai Arrow gets emotional farewell 100th NRL appearance for South Sydney Rabbitohs after Motor Neurone Disease diagnosis | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to content Jai Arrow gets emotional farewell 100th NRL appearance for South Sydney Rabbitohs after Motor Neurone Disease diagnosis Jai Arrow retired from rugby league in May following an MND diagnosis; NRL gave South Sydney Rabbitohs special dispensation to include Arrow in their squad and feature as an extra player for the last two matches of the regular season, allowing him to pass 100 appearances for the club Friday 4 September 2026 14:47, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player South Sydney Rabbitohs player Jai Arrow receives an emotional welcome as he leads out the side for the last time after his MND diagnosis Jai Arrow made an emotional 100th NRL appearance for the South Sydney Rabbitohs to mark his farewell from the sport, following his Motor Neurone Disease diagnosis. Special dispensation had been granted by the NRL and Rabbitohs to allow Arrow the opportunity to take to the field for the opening kick-off another two times, with the game against Sydney Roosters marking a century of appearances. Arrow walked his team out onto the field for the Sydney derby, with 'Stand By Me' playing before 'You'll Never Walk Alone' then rang around the Allianz Stadium. metadata.summary: The Scottish FA is proposing financial incentives for clubs to play more young home-grown footballers.
metadata.content: Scottish FA summit: SPFL clubs to be offered incentives to play more home-grown youth players | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Scottish FA summit: SPFL clubs to be offered incentives to play more home-grown youth players Plans are designed to create more playing opportunities for young talent across every level of the SPFL; clubs will vote on the options when they gather at the SFA General Meeting in October and the SPFL’s AGM in November; if approved, they will come into force from next season Friday 4 September 2026 17:52, UK Image: Sam Cleall-Harding, James Wilson and Findlay Curtis all play in the Scottish Premiership and for Scotland U21s The Scottish FA is proposing financial incentives for clubs to play more young home-grown footballers. The governing body has announced £1m would be made available to clubs to incentivise increased game time for under-21 Scotland-eligible players.
